docs.text: AI proposal review integration The workflow lives in AI4S-Bench/ai4s-benchmark , the repository hosting proposal Discussions. The backend stores AI recommendations independently of human Proposal.review_* fields and approval status. Full Sync ignores the AI marker, even if a model quotes a human-review template. Configuration Deploy migration 20260924_0017 , the API and the job runner before enabling the benchmark workflow. Configure these backend settings in the protected environment: Setting Value TBCP_GITHUB_REPOSITORY AI4S-Bench/ai4s-benchmark TBCP_AI_REVIEW_SERVICE_KEY Independent random secret, at least 32 characters TBCP_AI_REVIEW_GITHUB_TOKEN Dedicated bot PAT with repository Discussions write access TBCP_DISCORD_WEBHOOK_URL Discord destination webhook TBCP_AI_REVIEW_DISCORD_FORUM true for a forum, false for a text channel TBCP_AI_REVIEW_SYNC_LABELS Optional, defaults to false Use a long-lived dedicated bot PAT for this implementation. A GitHub App installation token can be supplied, but automatic token minting/refresh is not implemented, so short-lived tokens require external rotation. The token owner must be able to edit its own Discussion comments. The OAuth cookie used by human reviewers is not involved. The service key is only accepted by the two internal AI review routes. It cannot access administrator or human-review APIs. Keys are read at runtime and are not stored in AI delivery payloads. Missing service authentication or publishing configuration fails closed. The AI model key is only needed in Actions. In the benchmark repository, configure: Secret LLM_API_KEY : selected OpenRouter account key. Secret AI_REVIEW_SERVICE_KEY : same value as the backend service key. Variable AI_REVIEW_BACKEND_URL : backend HTTPS origin, e.g. https://dashboard.ai4sbench.org . The current model is dots-studio/dots-3-note-preview:free at https://openrouter.ai/api/v1 . The script uses the synthetic openai/ prefix solely to select the upstream SDK; OpenRouter receives the exact selected model ID. There is no paid fallback. API POST /api/v1/internal/proposal-ai-reviews , authenticated with Authorization: Bearer <service-key> , accepts AIReviewSubmission (see OpenAPI). { "schema_version": "ai4sbench-proposal-ai-review/v1", "repository": "AI4S-Bench/ai4s-benchmark", "discussion_number": 33, "discussion_node_id": "D_example", "run_id": 123456, "run_attempt": 1, "workflow_sha": "aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa", "upstream_sha": "f55c14ea065243c8d094e02c0aa156d5fd22fdd4", "model": "dots-studio/dots-3-note-preview:free", "proposal_digest": "<sha256 of title + newline + body>", "status": "completed", "result": { "decision": "Accept", "review": "Full rubric review in Markdown", "summary": "Review summary", "author_fit": null, "coi": null } } unavailable requires result: null ; provider errors are never rendered into public comments. Completed results must use the original TBS five-level decision enum. The backend verifies Discussion identity, category and content digest using GitHub, and checks deletion tombstones. A local Proposal row need not exist yet; AI records join to proposals using the Discussion node ID, including after Full Sync. Response 202 contains review_id , publication_id , and each destination's delivery ID/state. It means persisted/queued, not externally published. GET /api/v1/internal/proposal-ai-reviews/{review_id} returns current states with the same service key. Operators also see AI jobs in the existing delivery dashboard. Identical callbacks for the same repository/run/attempt return the existing record. Conflicting content returns 409. A newer accepted run supersedes older queued publications; old callbacks return 409. A rerun of an older run does not replace a newer run. During an active publication lease, new ingestion returns 503 with Retry-After: 10 ; the workflow retries. No SQLite transaction spans network I/O. Changed proposal content or deletion blocks pending publication. Repeat /review with write/admin permissions to produce a fresh review after editing a proposal. Delivery and recovery GitHub gets one bot-owned sticky comment; Discord gets one review message/forum thread updated on later reviews. Human comments and the initial proposal Discord announcement are unchanged. A GitHub retry searches all Discussion-comment pages for the AI marker owned by the publishing bot, which recovers a lost create response. A different author's marker is never adopted or edited. The bot must retain its identity and permissions across deployments. Each channel retries independently. A Discord retry does not republish GitHub. Known Discord message IDs are PATCHed. Explicit rejection such as HTTP 429 can retry creation. A timeout, server error or process crash during initial creation is ambiguous: the job stops rather than automatically creating a duplicate. An administrator can reconcile an uncertain initial send via: POST /api/v1/ai-review-publications/{publication_id}/recover-discord Use the normal administrator session. If the message exists, submit its ID and forum thread ID: {"message_id": "123456789", "thread_id": "987654321"} The backend fetches it using the configured webhook and verifies its AI-review footer. It then queues an update. For a regular text channel omit thread_id . Only after inspecting Discord and confirming no message was created, submit: {"confirmed_not_sent": true} This clears the uncertainty flag and requeues the latest Discord job. Ordinary Resend cannot bypass the uncertainty guard. Do not rotate to a different webhook channel while pending deliveries exist; old message IDs belong to the old webhook. Administrators assign a proposal reviewer from the dashboard. Eligible reviewers have an approved application, a GitHub login, and at least one domain in common with the proposal; the author is excluded. The free-text field is displayed to help the administrator decide, but is not an exact-match filter. Assignments are stored on the proposal separately from submitted human reviews. A change to an existing AI review publication queues an update to its GitHub sticky comment; later AI review reruns read the same manual assignment. Optional labels reflect current author-fit; COI disclosure is add-only. No AI label changes human approval status. Missing optional labels are skipped. Verification and operational limits Backend: uv run pytest and uv run ruff check control_panel tests . Migration: uv run alembic upgrade head against a disposable SQLite database. Benchmark: python -m unittest discover -s ci_checks -p test_proposal_review.py . Workflow: actionlint .github/workflows/proposal-review.yml .github/workflows/proposal-review-tests.yml . Live smoke test after deployment: new proposal, authorized/unauthorized /review , dispatch, model failure, Discord failure and a successful rerun updating both messages. For the proposal-to-review path, run the opt-in live test from the repository root: $env:AI_REVIEW_LIVE = "1" python backend/tests/test_live_ai_review_e2e.py It uses GITHUB_TOKEN or GH_TOKEN , falling back to the locally authenticated gh token. It publishes a public Task Proposals Discussion, waits up to 20 minutes for a completed AI review comment, and verifies the linked Actions run. To resume without creating another Discussion, set AI_REVIEW_E2E_DISCUSSION_NUMBER to the number printed by the first run. This test intentionally writes to production. The free endpoint is text-only. Image links remain in the proposal but are not fetched, and published reviews disclose this limitation. The runner conservatively bounds combined rubric/input to 28,000 UTF-8 bytes to reserve output space inside the endpoint's 32,768-token context; oversized proposals produce an unavailable review. Empty/truncated model output also produces an unavailable review. The optional author-fit pass can fail without suppressing a valid primary review. Workflow artifacts retain result, proposal and sanitized diagnostics for seven days. A failed backend callback fails Actions and preserves those artifacts. Publishing remains asynchronous; inspect backend delivery state after Actions acceptance. Disabling the workflow or service key stops new ingestion, while already queued publication continues until the job runner is stopped. Validation note The repository-wide alembic check already reports differences in the original user , oauth_account and proposals metadata at the inspected baseline commit. This change does not alter those tables. The focused migration regression checks both new AI tables against their models, downgrades to 20260924_0016 , and upgrades again while preserving the existing outbound-delivery table.

docs.text: Architecture and Ownership Application composition src/main.py builds the FastAPI application, mounts the domain routers, serves the committed Dashboard and Website assets, and configures lifecycle behavior. src/api_docs.py publishes separate OpenAPI contracts so each public API surface can evolve without relying on the combined legacy schema. The backend has three main areas: Area Owns Key code Community Proposals, reviewer applications, reviews, GitHub synchronization, and outbound deliveries src/community/ Control panel Benchmark plans and runs, execution backends, task data, and worker-facing APIs src/control_panel/ Shared runtime Configuration, authentication, database sessions/models, and cross-domain jobs src/core/ , src/db/ , src/jobs/ Community and control-panel schemas and services belong to their domains. The database is shared. src/jobs/runner.py orchestrates queued community and v1 work; Harbor v2 has its own runner under src/control_panel/v2/ . API contracts The current separately versioned API surfaces are: Surface Swagger UI OpenAPI JSON Community v1 /docs/community/v1 /openapi/community/v1.json EC2 control panel v1 /docs/ec2/v1 /openapi/ec2/v1.json Harbor EC2 v2 /docs/ec2/v2 /openapi/ec2/v2.json /docs and /openapi.json remain the combined legacy surface for existing consumers. When changing an API, update the owning schema/route and its contract-level documentation together. Persistence and migrations ORM models and database session setup live under src/db/ . Alembic settings are in alembic.ini ; versioned schema changes live in migrations/versions/ . Do not treat a model-only change as a complete schema change: add and review a migration, and keep upgrade behavior aligned with supported existing databases. Frontend assets Dashboard source is in dashboard-frontend/frontend/ ; its Vite build is committed to src/static/ . The public Website source is the ai4s-bench-website/ submodule, while its deployable snapshot is src/website_dist/ . Follow the build and submodule workflow in backend/README.md when updating either asset set. Change checklist For a behavior change, identify the owning domain, update the route/schema or service, review persistence and migrations if data changes, and update this wiki when the interface or operational behavior changes. Existing tests under tests/ document many integration contracts; add or adjust coverage with the implementation change.

docs.text: Model / Schema Consistency Audit Audit date: 2026-10-13 (baseline branch audit; latest-main follow-up noted below) Scope: SQLAlchemy models, Pydantic request/response schemas, API route transformations, website proposal/task lifecycle contract, Alembic migrations, and a read-only snapshot of the deployed SQLite database. Method: static comparison of model fields, schemas and route payload construction; review of migration chain; read-only production queries ( quick_check , enum/value checks, relationship/document checks). No production data was changed. Current contract update (2026-10-18): The proposal PR guide now derives tasks/<primary-domain>/<task-slug>/ and task/<primary-domain>-<task-slug> . field remains proposal metadata and is no longer a task-path segment. The findings below describe the dated baseline audit and are retained as history. Executive summary The highest-risk inconsistency is in proposal taxonomy: the proposal accepts multiple human-readable domains, but the PR guide interpolates that combined value directly into a repository path. This can yield an invalid tasks/<domain>/<field>/<slug> path. The proposal form's domain list also does not match the AI review rubric's scientific scope (tracked upstream as Issues #44 and #46 ). Proposal, human-review, reviewer-application, and AI-review decision/status enums are shared between ORM and Pydantic where they represent the same vocabulary. Operational run/job/delivery states are less consistently constrained: most are plain strings, while selected schemas use Literal . Outbound delivery type is the clearest model/schema contract gap. The public task lifecycle is a separate derived vocabulary and should remain explicitly documented as a projection of proposal/review/revision evidence. The production snapshot had no observed invalid proposal/reviewer/review enum values or review-column/document drift. The deployed DB was at Alembic revision 20261013_0020 ; local revision 20261013_0021 adds enum checks and therefore had not yet been applied at the time of the snapshot. Findings A1 — Proposal domain is not safe to use as a task-directory segment — High ProposalSubmission.domain accepts a comma-separated list, canonicalizes it as readable labels, and does not validate entries against the selectable domain list. The PR-instructions route then uses proposal.domain verbatim in tasks/{domain}/{field}/{task_slug} and in the branch name. A multi-domain value such as Biology, AI / ML therefore becomes multiple path components and includes spaces/punctuation. Even a single readable label such as Materials Science does not match the benchmark repository's lowercase hyphenated directory convention. This is an implementation-level contract mismatch, not just missing documentation. Evidence: backend/src/community/schemas.py ( PROPOSAL_DOMAIN_OPTIONS , ProposalSubmission.normalize_domain_list ); backend/src/community/routes.py:1390-1391 (branch/path construction); upstream Issue #44 . Impact: contributors can receive a PR guide that points to a non-existent/non-conforming folder. Persisting display labels in Proposal.domain also means a future path fix needs an explicit canonical slug or a deterministic primary-domain rule. Recommendation: settle the allowed scientific domain/field taxonomy first; store structured selected domains separately from a single canonical task-directory domain and field slug. Generate repository paths only from validated canonical identifiers. Decide the primary-folder rule for genuinely cross-domain proposals and document task.toml metadata keys alongside it. A2 — Proposal form, AI rubric, and task taxonomy have different scopes — High / policy decision The API publishes seven selectable labels: Materials Science, Physics, Chemistry, Biology, AI / ML, Applied Mathematics, and Interdisciplinary. The review rubric describes the covered sciences as life, physical, earth, mathematical, and engineering sciences, and says an in-scope method such as ML does not make an out-of-scope subject in-scope. Earth and engineering sciences are absent from the form; AI / ML and Interdisciplinary are selectable as if they were scientific domains. field_name is free text and field_slug is generated mechanically, but there is no canonical mapping from form labels/fields to repository folder slugs or task metadata. Evidence: backend/src/community/schemas.py ( PROPOSAL_DOMAIN_OPTIONS , ProposalSubmission.field_name , field_slug ); upstream rubric task-proposal.md ; Issues #44 and #46 . Impact: applicant-facing categories do not reliably predict AI-review scope decisions or the task's eventual directory. A task may be accepted/rejected based on its actual subject while the form's primary label suggests a different policy. Recommendation: treat #44 and #46 as one taxonomy decision. Decide whether categories denote scientific subject, methods, or cross-cutting tags; align the form, reviewer rubric, folder taxonomy, task.toml , and API model in one change. Do not make a code-only slug mapping until that policy is agreed. A3 — Delivery contract is stricter in Pydantic than in the ORM — Medium OutboundDelivery.delivery_type and OutboundDelivery.state are unrestricted SQLAlchemy strings. OutboundDeliveryResponse.delivery_type only permits discord , github_discussion , or smtp , while its state is an unrestricted string. Thus ORM/database writes can create a delivery type that cannot be serialized by the admin response schema. The mailing-specific response independently constrains state to pending | sending | completed | failed , but that response is a projection of the same durable delivery workflow and does not constrain the database column. Evidence: backend/src/db/models.py ( OutboundDelivery ); backend/src/community/schemas.py ( OutboundDeliveryResponse ); backend/src/mailing/schemas.py ( MailingDeliveryResponse ); backend/src/community/admin_routes.py and backend/src/mailing/routes.py response models. Impact: unsupported delivery type values can cause response validation failures; unknown states can pass through to callers and UI code without an explicit contract. Multiple independently maintained vocabularies can drift. Recommendation: define shared string enums for delivery type and durable delivery state, use them in model and schemas, and keep any response-specific subset as a separately named projection if it is intentional. Verify that all existing values are represented before adding database constraints. A4 — Operational lifecycle states have uneven validation strength — Medium / consistency debt ExecutionPlan.state , Run.state , DatabaseJob.state , OutboundDelivery.state , HarborRunV2.state , and User.role are stored as strings. Their schemas vary: v1 plan/run/job responses use str ; Harbor v2 response uses a Literal ; worker completion accepts only succeeded | failed ; mailing response uses a four-value Literal ; AuthenticatedUserResponse.role uses str . This is not evidence that the stored rows are currently wrong, but the ORM does not reject typos and a few response surfaces enforce vocabularies that other surfaces do not. Evidence: backend/src/db/models.py ; backend/src/control_panel/v2/models.py ; backend/src/core/identity.py ; backend/src/control_panel/schemas.py ; backend/src/control_panel/v2/schemas.py ; backend/src/community/schemas.py ; backend/src/mailing/schemas.py . Recommendation: inventory the actual transition graphs before enum-typing these columns. Then share enums for persisted finite state machines (plan, run, job, delivery, user role) across SQLAlchemy and Pydantic. Keep provider-reported Run.instance_state separate because its vocabulary is owned by AWS and may evolve independently. Worker completion can remain a narrower command schema if that is deliberate. A5 — Proposal status vs public lifecycle status is a dual vocabulary and should be made explicit — Low / documentation The ORM/Pydantic proposal status enum is draft | pending | approved | changes_requested | rejected . The website also displays derived values such as implementation , agent_testing , and released based on review columns and task-revision data. The frontend explicitly describes this derivation: it combines status , review_* , and revision_* because proposal status alone does not represent downstream work. This is a valid read-model design, but clients may mistake the display status for a persisted proposal status. The website's site.json additionally uses editorial labels such as proposed / under_review . Evidence: backend/src/core/enums.py ( ProposalStatus ); backend/src/community/schemas.py ( ProposalBoardItemResponse ); ai4s-bench-website/js/lifecycle.js ( displayStatus , STATUS_INFO ); ai4s-bench-website/data/site.json ( statuses ). Recommendation: name and document the API's persisted proposal status separately from the website's derived task lifecycle status. Maintain one explicit mapping/projection test when additional workflow stages become live. A6 — Email-verification gap in the baseline branch was resolved on latest main At the baseline branch revision audited above, migration 20261013_0020 created email_verification_challenges but there was no ORM model or application code using it. docs.text: The highest-risk inconsistency is in proposal taxonomy: the proposal accepts multiple human-readable domains, but the PR guide interpolates that combined value directly into a repository path. docs.text: ProposalSubmission.domain accepts a comma-separated list, canonicalizes it as readable labels, and does not validate entries against the selectable domain list. The PR-instructions route then uses proposal.domain verbatim in tasks/{domain}/{field}/{task_slug} and in the branch name. A multi-domain value such as Biology, AI / ML therefore becomes multiple path components and includes spaces/punctuation. Even a single readable label such as Materials Science does not match the benchmark repository's lowercase hyphenated directory convention. This is an implementation-level contract mismatch, not just missing documentation. Evidence: backend/src/community/schemas.py ( PROPOSAL_DOMAIN_OPTIONS , ProposalSubmission.normalize_domain_list ); backend/src/community/routes.py:1390-1391 (branch/path construction); upstream Issue #44 . Impact: contributors can receive a PR guide that points to a non-existent/non-conforming folder. Persisting display labels in Proposal.domain also means a future path fix needs an explicit canonical slug or a deterministic primary-domain rule. Recommendation: settle the allowed scientific domain/field taxonomy first; store structured selected domains separately from a single canonical task-directory domain and field slug. Generate repository paths only from validated canonical identifiers. Decide the primary-folder rule for genuinely cross-domain proposals and document task.toml metadata keys alongside it.

docs.text: The API publishes seven selectable labels: Materials Science, Physics, Chemistry, Biology, AI / ML, Applied Mathematics, and Interdisciplinary. The review rubric describes the covered sciences as life, physical, earth, mathematical, and engineering sciences, and says an in-scope method such as ML does not make an out-of-scope subject in-scope. Earth and engineering sciences are absent from the form; AI / ML and Interdisciplinary are selectable as if they were scientific domains. field_name is free text and field_slug is generated mechanically, but there is no canonical mapping from form labels/fields to repository folder slugs or task metadata. Evidence: backend/src/community/schemas.py ( PROPOSAL_DOMAIN_OPTIONS , ProposalSubmission.field_name , field_slug ); upstream rubric task-proposal.md ; Issues #44 and #46 . Impact: applicant-facing categories do not reliably predict AI-review scope decisions or the task's eventual directory. A task may be accepted/rejected based on its actual subject while the form's primary label suggests a different policy. Recommendation: treat #44 and #46 as one taxonomy decision. Decide whether categories denote scientific subject, methods, or cross-cutting tags; align the form, reviewer rubric, folder taxonomy, task.toml , and API model in one change. Do not make a code-only slug mapping until that policy is agreed.

docs.text: OutboundDelivery.delivery_type and OutboundDelivery.state are unrestricted SQLAlchemy strings. The mailing-specific response independently constrains state to pending | sending | completed | failed , but that response is a projection of the same durable delivery workflow and does not constrain the database column. Recommendation: define shared string enums for delivery type and durable delivery state, use them in model and schemas, and keep any response-specific subset as a separately named projection if it is intentional. Verify that all existing values are represented before adding database constraints.

slug；目前没有发布有限的 <domain>/<field> 配对清单，也没有在 API 入口校验领域必须来自这七项。 Benchmark 的 scripts/validate_task.py 要求五个任务文件、可解析的 [metadata] 表；存在 [task] 时要求其 name 是 org/name 。新任务 PR 须链接本仓库的提案 Discussion。该校验器 不 检查领域是否属于表单选项，也不强制 [metadata].domain 或 [metadata].field 。 已确定的范围口径： 当前七个表单标签就是新提案的准入领域；让 AI review rubric 跟随表单，而不是用 rubric 原有的五类科学范围替换表单。 AI / ML 和 Interdisciplinary 也属于这七项，但仍须满足 rubric 对真实研究工作、领域知识、可验证性的其他要求。地球或工程科学如果不能真实归入这七项之一，目前不作为新的独立准入领域。rubric 文字、例子和实际审查行为尚需在后续分支落实；在落实前，不应声称 #46 已由代码解决。 由当前七项按后台现有 slug 规则生成的 新任务主领域目录 为 materials-science 、 physics 、 chemistry 、 biology 、 ai-ml 、 applied-mathematics 、 interdisciplinary 。这不是对历史目录的迁移要求，例如已有 mathematical-sciences/applied-mathematics 示例仍保留。新提案的研究 field 继续由自由文本生成 slug，不能把它误写为现已存在的有限 field 清单。 已确定的 metadata 口径： 新任务只使用 [metadata].domain 与 [metadata].field 表达目录分类，分别与任务路径的两个目录段一致；不再为新任务生成或校验 [metadata].category 。例如 tasks/physics/inverse-problems/<task-slug>/task.toml 应包含： [metadata] domain = "physics" field = "inverse-problems" 现有示例的 category 是旧写法，后续分支会把示例改成这两个键。旧任务无需因该文档决定而批量改写；校验器新增强制规则时只对 新任务 要求两个键，避免维修历史任务时意外阻断。 各 PR 的处理 条目 核对结果 处理方式 Website PR #34 把预检中的 [metadata] 解析、 [task].name 、新任务 Discussion 链接及目录识别向 benchmark CI 对齐；还修正测试样例，把旧 category 放回 [metadata] 并补上 [task].name 。这是 结构校验 ，不决定领域准入表。指南的一处措辞把 [task].name 写成无条件必需，而当前 CI 是“存在 [task] 时必需”。 独立审阅；可建议贡献者将指南措辞改为与 CI 一致。核心结构校验可保留；后续分支应将旧样例的分类键改为 domain / field 、检查 Website 当前主分支差异和资源版本号，再让预检与更新后的 CI 对齐。不要用 #44/#46 的理由直接拒绝。 Benchmark PR #38 说明 CI 已要求 [metadata] 表，和当前 validate_task.py 相符；没有规定领域键的最终格式。 可作为独立文档修正审阅。后续确定 metadata 的具体字段后，再补充规范；当前 PR 无须等待 #44/#46 才能判断。 Benchmark PR #56 将贡献文档中的 <task-name> 改为 <task-slug> ，与 CONTRIBUTING.md 的目录占位符一致；不改变允许的领域。 可作为独立文档修正审阅。后续另行补充主领域到目录的映射说明。 这三条 PR 的作者均为 chenyangsu ；感谢其指出真实的校验和文档偏差。是否合并应依据各自的实际 diff，而不是套用同一条“因新领域设计无法合并”的回复。 category 与 domain / field 的实际用途 [metadata].category 用一个字符串表达两层目录，例如 mathematical-sciences/applied-mathematics 。在本项目当前代码中，它只出现在 benchmark 示例任务的 task.toml 和 Website 的测试样例；任务运行、后台及 benchmark CI 没有依据它进行分类或校验。新的规范不使用这个键。 Website 指南的模板已经使用两个独立键： [metadata].domain 对应 <domain> 目录， [metadata].field 对应 <field> 目录。Website 预检在这两个键存在时逐项比对目录，不一致时给 警告 ；benchmark CI 尚未要求这两个键，也不检查 category 。后续分支将把新任务的两个字段及其目录一致性纳入 CI，并使预检保持一致。 GitHub Discussion 的 category = Task Proposals 是 Discussion 所在的 GitHub 分类，与 task.toml 的 [metadata].category 无关。 首次核对时 #44 / #46 的剩余工作 问题 当前状态 后续分支需要落实 多领域提案放哪个任务目录 首项为主领域并用于路径，已在后台和 Website 实现 在 benchmark 贡献文档与 Website 指南写明同一规则；给出示例及对历史路径的兼容说明。 哪些目录 slug 可用 七个表单标签可以机械生成主领域 slug；field 仍为自由文本 公布七个主领域标签及其 slug，以及 field slug 的生成规则和审核责任；若希望有限 field 清单，须另作设计决定。 科学准入范围 已决定保留表单当前七类作为准入领域，但当前 rubric 仍列 life / physical / earth / mathematical / engineering 修改 rubrics/task-proposal.md 的 Scope、例子和审查提示；明确 AI / ML 与 Interdisciplinary 也可作为领域，但仍需真实研究内容。删除把地球/工程列为独立准入领域的旧表述。 task.toml 的领域 metadata 已决定新任务只用 [metadata].domain / [metadata].field ；现有示例仍用 category ，CI 只检查表存在 把示例改为两个新键；仅对新任务要求它们与目录一致，Website 预检和 CI 同步执行。历史任务无需批量改写。 首次核对时建议的收尾顺序 在 rubric 的 Scope 中写清七类准入、主领域及 AI / ML 、 Interdisciplinary 的研究要求。 在后续分支一次性对齐 rubric、benchmark 贡献文档、任务示例、Website 指南与预检，并让新提案的领域校验符合七类选择。保持提案表中的逗号分隔字段；新增任务使用 domain / field ，旧任务保留原样。 分别审阅 #34、#38、#56，并在对应 PR 下回复具体处理意见；不要把三条独立修正当成 #44/#46 的实现 PR。 发布规则后，在 #44/#46 下链接实现分支与文档，核对新提案到任务路径及 task.toml 的完整示例，再决定关闭 Issue。 本记录的边界： 这是处理方案与状态核对，不代表 rubric、benchmark 仓库或 Website 上游已合并相应改动，也不代替逐条 PR 的代码审查。
